Press Release: January 21, 2025                                      
           
SCBX ANNOUNCED YEARLY NET PROFIT OF BAHT 43,943 MILLION, 
with a strong financial position and prudent asset quality management. 
 
Bangkok: SCB X Public Company Limited (SCBX) has reported a consolidated net profit of Baht 43,943 million 
for the year 2024, a 1.0% yoy increase. For the last quarter of the year, the net profit was Baht 11,707 million, 
a 6.5% yoy increase.  
For 2024, net interest income increased by 3.8% yoy to Baht 129,424 million, resulting from an expansion in 
the net interest margin (NIM) while overall loans dropped slightly by 1.0% yoy as a r esult of prudent new loan 
underwriting. Fee and other income declined by 5.6% yoy to Baht 40,657 million, mainly due to a decrease in 
bancassurance fees and lending-related fees.  
Operating expenses increased by 1.7% yoy to Baht 72,977 million. The cost-to-income ratio was at 42.3%. 
The provisions decreased by 2.3% yoy, mainly due to consistently prudent and careful asset quality 
management. The non-performing loan (NPL) coverage ratio remained high at 158%. 
The overall asset quality is well under control. The NPL ratio was 3.37% at the end of 2024, slightly lower than 
the 3.44% recorded at the end of last year. The capital adequacy ratio remained strong at 18.9%.  
 
Arthid Nanthawithaya, Chief Executive Officer of SCBX, commented: 
"The year 2024 was a challenging year in many dimensions, both economicall y and technologically. The 
SCBX Group aimed for cautious business growth, prudently managing asset quality an d focusing on 
strengthening financial stability. Additionally, the Company established Poi ntX as a central platform to 
enhance customer engagement within the Group. SCBX has received official validation of its near-term 
science-based greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets from the Science Based  Targets initiative 
(SBTi), becoming the first financial institution in Thailand to receiv e this validation, aiming for a Net Zero 
target by 2050 and sustainable growth. 
In 2025, SCBX will focus on continuous growth from our existing businesses, parti cularly in the consumer 
finance, by efficiently managing costs and improving debt collection processes. The Company will also fully 
support vulnerable customer groups under government measures. 
SCBX prioritizes sustainable growth by preparing to collaborate with business partners to establish a Virtual 
Bank and aiming for Net Zero targets. The Company will also explore growth opportunities in Climate Tech. 
Furthermore, SCBX is progressing towards becoming an AI-first organization by integrating AI into all 
aspects of operations to enhance efficiency and meet evolving customer needs.”

Executive Summary  
 
2024 was another challenging year due to the Thai economy performing worse than anticip ated.  
Various factors, including geopolitical conflicts and domestic structural issues,  have hinder ed the 
economy’s ability to gain momentum. Additionally, the high level of household debt has led to cautious 
spending and borrowing behaviors.  
SCBX demonstrated resilience with a net profit of Baht 43.9 billion in 2024, slightl y higher than the 
previous year. Despite economic challenges, the Company maintained balance sheet stability, ensured 
effective cost control and improved productivity. The main income growth was driven by 12 bps NIM 
rise yoy as SCB Bank enjoyed the full-year benefit of the policy rate hikes in 2023 and Gen 2 companies 
contributed positively, even though overall loan growth was muted. Fee income was down 5.6% yoy, 
primarily due to reduced bancassurance fees and lending-related fees, both impacted by unfavorable 
business sentiment. Cost control continued to be robust with overall CI ratio at 42.3 %. Asset quality 
remained a key focus, with close monitoring, especially in the weak pocket of retail  segment. Credit 
cost slightly declined from last year to 176 bps with main improvement from Ge n 2 business. As such, 
Gen 2 business is back on track of profitability turnaround.   
The Company has taken strategic steps to lay foundation for long-term growth as well as preserve 
capital. Firstly, we have entered into the Share Purchase Agreement to acquire 100 %-stake in Home 
Credit Vietnam, a leading consumer finance company in Vietnam. This deal is still subject to regulatory 
approvals. Secondly, we decided to exit Purple Ventures, a portfolio company that operates loss-making 
Robinhood food delivery platform. While we incurred Baht 1.5 billion one-time net divestment loss during 
the year, such strategic move will be positive for the group’s profitability goi ng forward with an option 
for up to Baht 1.6 billion profit sharing if Purple Ventures turns profitable under t he new owner. Lastly, 
we have formed partnership with Kakao Bank and WeBank, both leading digital banks in the region, to 
apply for the Virtual Banking license in Thailand. The outcome of the license application is expected by 
around mid of 2025.

2 
 
For 2025, SCBX has established performance targets against the backdrop of soft economic recovery 
and one policy rate cut. These targets include loan growth of 1-3%, net interest margin of 3.6-3.8%, net 
fee income growth of 2-4%, cost to income ratio of 42-44%, and credit cost of 150-170bps.  
 
2024 operating performance 
 
In 2024, SCBX reported a consolidated net profit of Baht 43.9 billion, a s light 1.0% increase from the 
previous year. This increase was primarily due to an increase in net interest i ncome, driven by an 
improved net interest margin (NIM) and lower expected credit losses. However, these gains were offset 
by one-off items from the Robinhood transaction, subdued fee income mainly from bancassurance and 
lending-related fees, and reduced investment income due to mark- to-market adjustments in the 
investment portfolio. 
In 2024, the Group effectively controlled costs, achieving a cost- to-income ratio of 41.7%, excluding 
the impact from the Robinhood transaction. Expected credit losses (ECL) decreased year-on-year to 
Baht 42.6 billion, equivalent to 1 76 basis points of total loans. This decline was primarily driven by 
improved ECL at CardX due to de-risking in the P-loan segment, while the EC L at the Bank slightly 
decreased due to the absence of additional provisions recorded in 2023.  
The Group’s loan growth declined slightly by 1.0% year- on-year, with reductions across all segments 
at SCB Bank and a decrease at CardX, as the focus shifted to quality customers. Meanwhil e, loans at 
AutoX and MONIX continued to grow, albeit at a slower pace. Asset quality remaine d relatively stable 
at 3.37%. The Group continued to proactively manage NPLs through effective sales and write- offs, 
while maintaining a high coverage ratio of 158.0%. 
In 4Q24, SCBX achieved a record high net profit of Baht 11.7 billion for the year, an increase of 6.5% 
yoy and 7.0% qoq. The y oy growth was primarily driven by higher investment and trading income, 
increased net fee income from wealth business and reduced operating expenses. For qoq comparison, 
NIM softened 3 bps given a policy rate cut in the quarter. Fee income on the other ha nd slightly 
improved 2% driven by wealth business. Investment income swang from net loss to net gain of Baht 
1.2 billion driven primarily by investment gain in SCB10X’s portfolio, especial ly investment in digital 
asset-related startups. Credit cost fell 18 bps qoq as overall asset quality, while still challenging, was in 
line with our expectation. 
 
2025 SCBX Strategy: Driving Growth, Efficiency, and Long-Term Value 
 
SCBX remains committed to its vision of becoming the “Most Admired Region al Financial Technology 
Group.” Building on our robust foundation, we have refined our strategic priorities for 2025 to focus on 
driving growth, enhancing operational efficiency, and creating long-term value for ou r stakeholders. 
These priorities are organized into four key pillars:

SCB X Public Company Limited  Management Discussion and Analysis 
 
3 
 
1. Driving Growth in Existing Businesses 
• Our focus for 2025 is on scaling our core businesses with a focus on debt collecti on to drive 
credit cost improvement while maintaining marginal loan growth and capturing fee i ncome 
opportunities. 
• Strengthening SCB Bank foundation as a core earnings contribution for the Group:  
o Improving credit cost through end-to-end portfolio quality enhancements and enhancing 
efficiency in collection processes as well as leveraging the government’s debt  
restructuring program “You Fight, We Help” to protect downside risks from low income 
segments. 
o Driving fee income growth, particularly in the wealth management segment, by offering 
new products and segments to fulfill all dimensions of customers' wealth aspirations and 
needs and using both conventional and AI tools to increase RMs (Relationship 
Managers) productivity 
o Adopting AI to optimize costs and unlock additional revenue streams. 
• Maximizing Contributions from Gen 2 Businesses: 
o CardX: Focusing on profitability turnaround by continuing to improve collection efficiency, 
enhancing customer engagement to drive fee income through higher credit card 
utilization, and prudently growing the loan book. CardX should be a key contributor to 
earnings for Gen 2 business this year.  
o AutoX: Continuing business expansion with a strategic shift toward a lower-risk portfolio 
mix while capturing additional revenue streams from fee income, such as insu rance 
sales. Cost efficiency remains at the heart of AutoX to drive low CI ratio and targeted 
ROA. 
o MONIX: Sustaining disciplined growth through prudent credit management and portfolio 
optimization process. MONIX will further refine credit scoring model to capture the best 
risk-reward profiles of customers and maximize bad debt recovery by proactive debt 
restructuring programs.  
2. Enhancing Cost Control and Operational Efficiency 
We recognize the importance of disciplined cost management in driving sustainable v alue. We put 
stringent cost control as the heart of our group-wide operations. Key initiatives in 2025 include:  
• Streamlining Operations with AI: Leveraging AI to enhance operational efficiency and drive 
productivity gains, ultimately reducing the cost- to-income (CI) ratio while unlocking new 
revenue opportunities. At present, we are implementing over 230 AI initiatives with group-wide 
impact cutting across all functions from front to back office.

SCB X Public Company Limited  Management Discussion and Analysis 
 
4 
 
3. Strategic Growth Initiatives and Asset Rationalization  
SCBX will take a disciplined approach to managing our portfolio and seizing  new opportunities for 
growth. 
• Investments in Strategic Businesses: 
o Home Credit Vietnam (HCVN): We continue to work with regulators to obtain approvals 
to acquire HCVN. We believe HCVN will deliver meaningful profit contributions, with 
potential upside from increased scale and more competitive funding cost. 
o Virtual Bank: We are in the process of applying for a Virtual Bank license. Upon 
approval, we aim to partner with our consortium members to develop a cutting-edge, 
digital-first banking platform. Our vision is to advance financial inclusion and capture new 
market opportunities, setting new benchmarks in digital banking innovation.  
• Asset Rationalization:  SCB 10X’s portfolio, along with select portfolio companies, will be 
strategically evaluated to maximize returns and preserve capital. 
 
4. Driving Group Synergy and Building a Foundation for the Future 
Our long-term growth depends on maximizing synergies across the Group and buildi ng capabilities to 
sustain cost advantage as well as be ready for future expansion when opportunity presents itself.  
• Group-Wide AI Adoption: To be AI-first organization, SCBX has been implementing various 
AI initiatives to enhance work efficiency. Group Data Zone (GDZ) which is  group-wide data 
infrastructure under DataX has become fully operational to accelerate AI adoption at SCBX. At 
the end of 2024, data with necessary consents from customers has been onboarded to the 
GDZ. There are over 4,000 data attributes per customer ranging from customer profile, 
behavioral data to early warning signals. In terms of GenAI deployment, SCBX has  launched 
Typhoon, a Thai-language Large Language Model (LLM), trained in-house on open-s ource 
base LLM. This initiative allows flexibility for SCBX to scale Thai-language GenAI use cases at 
significantly lower cost than off- the-shelf solutions and with high degree of customization. 
Currently, our AI initiatives can be categorized into 4 groups as follows: 
• Cost Efficiency : This group focuses on enhancing operational efficiency and optimizing 
processes. The key initiatives include the Collection Strategy and Optimization, Bal ance 
Sheet Optimization, and the Enhanced Credit Risk Management Process. Meanwhile, t he 
portfolio company has implemented Streamlined Risk Management through the us e of 
Copilot and automation technologies. 
• Revenue Uplift: This group focuses on leveraging AI to help generating more revenue. Key 
initiatives include the Target Marketing and Sales AI Assistant implemented across products 
for retail customers by the portfolio companies, as well as the Intelligent Promotion Assistant 
developed by the portfolio companies.

• Customer Services: This group aims to enhance customer experience and support using 
AI-driven solutions. Portfolio company has introduced the AI-Augmented Collector Agent  
Call Assessment and has implemented AI-Enabled Investment Analysis. 
• Regulatory Compliance:  This group ensures adherence to regulatory requirements 
through advanced AI tools. Portfolio company focuses on Market Conduct compliance and 
employs Market Risk and News Monitoring AI tools. 
• Strengthening PointX as Group loyalty platform: PointX, launched in Nov-24, will be the key 
tool to grow customer lifetime value and build group-level loyalty, by trans forming the ways 
SCBX engages and nurtures customers, such as using AI to offer more personalized 
recommendations and having more exclusive perks for most active users. PointX wil l prioritize 
on long-term value creation and sustainable growth, ensuring the platform remains cost-
effective. 
 
Portfolio companies update 
2024 Performance and 2025 Action Plans  
 
SCB Bank  
 
In 2024, Siam Commercial Bank (SCB Bank) advanced its "Digital Bank w ith Human Touch" strategy 
by integrating advanced digital technologies with personalized customer service. T he Bank leveraged 
data and AI to swiftly analyze customer needs, delivering tailored solutions through stable and secure 
digital platforms. This approach contributed to a 15% growth in core wealth revenue.  
Despite challenges such as high household debt and global geopolitical uncertainti es, SCB Bank 
achieved its revenue and net profit targets. Net interest income expanded year-over-year, driven by  a 
high-interest-rate environment, though this was partially offset by loan contraction and a flight to quality.  
The Bank maintained a cost- to-income ratio of 38.5%, reflecting outstanding productivity through lean 
operations, cost control measures, and the adoption of digitalization, automation, and AI. This efficiency 
was further demonstrated by effective asset quality management and stringent risk control. 
In 2025, the Bank will continue to implement its "Digital Bank with Human Touch"  strategy, 
positioning itself as a "Universal Digital Bank that leads in wealth manageme nt while providing 
seamless and integrated service experiences across all channels for its customers."   These 
targeted actions for 2025 are designed to reinforce  SCB's position as a leading digital bank, driving 
sustainable growth and delivering value to its customers. 
1. Enhancing Wealth Management Services:  The Bank plans to expand fee income by 
adopting a customer goal-driven advisory framework,  boosting relationship manager 
productivity, and targeting existing SME business owners.

SCB X Public Company Limited  Management Discussion and Analysis 
 
6 
 
2. Maintaining Credit Portfolio Quality: The Bank will prioritize high-quality corporate loans in 
strategic industries and optimize its retail loan por tfolio. For mortgages, SCB Bank aims to 
sustain leadership with top developers while pursuin g selective growth in other segments. In 
auto loans, the focus will be on stabilizing the portfolio by winding down low-quali ty loans and 
targeting selective growth and new loans in major brands and premium segments.  
3. Improving Collection Efficiency and Recovery: SCB Bank intends to expedite repossession 
and litigation processes, leveraging AI and data analytics to enhance underwriting, collec tion, 
and recovery efforts. 
4. Enhancing Cost Efficiency: The Bank aims to boost employee productivity and ens ure 
prudent management of IT costs and investments. 
5. Strengthening Core Capabilities as an AI-First Bank : SCB Bank is committed to 
embedding AI across operations, building a robust d ata foundation, advancing process 
automation, and modernizing core banking systems to improve efficiency and service delivery. 
 
CardX 
 
In 2024, CardX delivered steady growth in net profit as the year progressed, reaching positive net 
profit in the second half of the year. Despite a ch allenging consumer credit outlook — reflected in 
weak consumer spending, high household debt, high N PLs, and low debt servicing ability —the 
Company maintained its bottom-line momentum by achi eving significant reduction in operating 
expenses and almost doubling recovery income from del inquent loan. In response to the challenging 
environment, CardX adopted a cautious approach by tightening underwriting criteria for new book ings 
and managing exposure to high-risk customer segment s. While this strategic approach reduced the 
loan balance, it resulted in a continuous improveme nt in asset quality, leading to the perf ormance 
turnaround. 
Throughout the year, CardX strengthened its foundat ion across key areas: risk management, 
collections, technology, and operations. The Compan y also integrated artificial intelligence (AI) into  
various business functions, including underwriting models and collection assessment. We deployed 
AI-powered chat bots and voice bots to assist in customer  service and debt collection, which has led 
to significant cost savings. Furthermore, risk manageme nt capabilities underwent an end - to-end 
transformation, leading to improved recovery perfor mance and other positive outcomes. During the 
fourth quarter, the Company executed credit card greenfield deployment on the new system to support 
technological readiness and to enhance customer service capabilities in the future. 
Heading into 2025, CardX strives to maintain its po sitive profitability momentum. CardX will focus on 
reinforcing its position in the credit card busines s by boosting card spending and increasing credit 
utilization. Additionally, CardX will expand its Ins talment Payment Plan (IPP) partnerships to drive 
growth and enhance customer engagement. These will translate into higher fee income for CardX.

SCB X Public Company Limited  Management Discussion and Analysis 
 
7 
 
CardX also aims to transform its collection process  by leveraging data analytics and adopting a 
segmentation-based approach. This will include enhan cing capabilities, workflows, and systems to 
improve collection effectiveness and reduce credit costs. Through these initiatives, CardX seeks 
further reduction in credit costs while maintaining a cautious  underwriting approach and ensuring risk 
management and collection effectiveness remain robust. 
The Company continue the plans to strategically red uce its exposure to personal loans, focusing on 
maintaining a balanced and profitable loan portfoli o. Furthermore, CardX will continue its efforts to 
optimize operating expenses (OPEX). Since 2Q24, over  40 cost optimization initiatives have been 
proposed and many already implemented, all aimed at driving OPEX reduction. 
By focusing on these strategic priorities, CardX remains committed to delivering excepti onal products 
and services, operational efficiency, and maintaining its leadership in risk ma nagement and collection 
excellence. These initiatives will contribute to th e Company’s profitability and sustainable growth in  
2025. 
 
AutoX  
 
In 2024, the auto title loan industry continued to grow, though at a slower pace than the previou s year, 
with early double-digit growth by market demand. However, AutoX is working to rebalance against 
higher credit risks stemming from a cautious macroeconomics environment.  
AutoX prioritized enhancing the productivity and efficiency of its 2,013 branches while ma intaining a 
disciplined approach toward operating expenses through partnership programs and optimizing 
utilization of staff. AutoX achieved a total loan book value of Baht 53 bill ion, representing a 56% year-
on-year increase. By focusing on the acquisition of new, quality customers and en gaging early with 
existing ones, AutoX limited its non-performing loan ratio to just 1.4% and continued to contribute profit 
to the SCBX Group.  
In addition to title loans, AutoX expanded its business into insurance brokerage serv ices, launching a 
nationwide campaign advertised on billboards in branches. This new offering was the first in the market 
to offer motor insurance under a 0%/24-month installment plan without requiring a credit card.   
In 2025, AutoX will pursue a sustainable growth strategy by shifting toward a high-qu ality portfolio that 
will include more land title and agricultural vehicle title loans to ensure  credit quality. By taking a 
disciplined and proactive approach toward collections, AutoX aims to maintain high asset quality. AutoX 
will focus on boosting non-interest income contributions from insurance fees by enha ncing branch 
capabilities for both life and non-life insurance sales. Lastly, AutoX aims  to continue increasing cost 
efficiency and productivity at both branches and back-office operations by implementing  AI and 
automation that will streamline daily operations and reduce routine workloads.

MONIX 
 
In 2024, MONIX reinforced the F.I.R.E. ecosystem by launching a “FINNIX Bonus” feature, designed to 
expand the nano-loan customer base through a referral incentive program for current customers. In  
addition, MONIX continued to provide free financial knowledge to help Thais to  improve their financial 
literacy by introducing a “Money Wise, Happy Life” online classroom. This sup ports our ecosystem's 
Empowerment pillar and aligns with the Responsible Lending Policy of the Bank of Thailand. 
MONIX continues to grow its register user base to over 5 million by implementing relevant campaigns 
such as “Confession of Loan Sharks” and other targeted initiatives. This strategic focus, combined with 
a 360-degree marketing approach, enabled the company to effectively reach underserved  customer 
segments nationwide, with particularly strong traction in key provincial cities.  
This momentum translated into exceptional results: 35% year- on-year loan growth, robust profitability, 
and efficient management of credit costs and operational expenses, even amidst a cha llenging credit 
environment. MONIX’s achievements were further underscored by three prestigious awards, 
highlighting its excellence in creative business, future enterprise leadership, and financial influence. 
Looking ahead to 2025, MONIX is committed to driving further growth by expanding its high-quality loan 
portfolio, enhancing product and service offerings, and maintaining effective cost controls. The company 
aims to solidify its position as the leading nano AI-lending platform in Thailand and achieve sustainable 
growth in the country’s digital credit market. 
 
InnovestX 
 
In 2024, navigating a challenging year marked by domestic economic instabili ty, InnovestX remained 
steadfast in its commitment to enhancing the investor experience. We focused on:  
• Elevating investor experience : We continued to refine our powerful trading tools, equipping 
them with comprehensive data and insights pooled together in our investment content hubs. 
This enriched platform caters to diverse investor preferences by offering an expansive product 
range that includes offshore investments such as stocks, mutual funds, private funds, a nd 
structured notes. 
• Strengthening institutional relationships: We solidified our position as a leading institutional 
brokerage house through strategic partnerships, unparalleled expertise, and strong client  
relationships. 
• Leveraging AI for enhanced advisory and services : Our Group’s advanced AI technology 
has significantly improved the efficiency and accuracy of our investment insights, empowering 
our clients to make informed decisions through AI-powered earnings briefs. Ad ditionally, we 
have developed AI-assisted digital relationship managers to enhance customer service, offering 
faster, more accurate, and human-like interactions.

SCB X Public Company Limited  Management Discussion and Analysis 
 
9 
 
As a result of these strategic initiatives, InnovestX achieved strong top-li ne growth, particularly in 
offshore-underlying products, while maintaining operational efficiency and strength ening our 
profitability. 
Despite the uncertain investment climate, InnovestX is poised for continued growth in 2025. We aim to 
progress by enhancing our end-to-end sales and services, providing personalized advisory, particularly 
for global investments, and continuously upgrading our trading tools. By prioritiz ing customer 
satisfaction and delivering exceptional service and support, we will strengthen our market position. 
Additionally, we will focus on improving operational efficiency to achieve higher, sustainable profitability. 
 
SCB 10X 
 
The market and economic conditions in 2024 show ed signs of recovery compared to 2023, especially 
in blockchain and digital assets. Our investment activities increased from the previous year, ending with 
a total of 14 investments. Exit activities doubled in 2024, with four exit events. Overall, SCB 10X’s 
investment portfolio stood at a fair value of US$483 million as of the fourth quarter of 2024 .  
In 2024, SCB 10X pursued its strategic priorities by: 1) Expanding our venture capital business with the 
launch of our second corporate VC fund (CVC), which focus es on AI and deep tech, 2) Transforming 
our venture building business into SCB 10X Tech Labs and SCB 10X R&D, and 3) Continuing to expand 
our regional presence and venture footprint. Under our first priority, we not only launched the new CVC 
fund but also expanded our network in AI by working closely with specialized funds and industry experts 
in this field. This led to successful deployment in seven AI companies, out of a total of 14 investments 
with 50% of the deals were co-invested with tier-1 investors.   
Under our second strategic priority, SCB 10X successfully pivoted its venture buil ding operations by 
establishing two distinct units, SCB 10X Tech Labs and SCB 10X R&D. SCB 10X  Tech Labs focuses 
on providing in-depth technical due diligence to the investment team, adding value  to portfolio 
companies via technical support, as well as showcasing our tech capabilities. A milestone achievement 
of SCB 10X Tech Labs was the launch of Rubie Wallet, a secure digital payment solution  for QR 
transactions based on conversion of USD and THB stablecoins, at Ethereum Foundation’s DevCon 
event in November 2024 under a regulatory sandbox approved by the Bank of Thailand and Thai SEC. 
At SCB 10X R&D, the team led AI advancements within the SCBX Group, w ith such highlights as the 
release of Typhoon, a series of open-source Thai large language models (LLMs), as well as 
collaborations and research publications with leading institutions like S tanford University and the 
University of Cambridge. 
As we venture into 2025, SCB 10X will continue our Moonshot Mission, with the as piration to be the 
leading investor in Southeast Asia and a tech leader in AI & blockchain. We are looking forward to 2025, 
continuing as the disruptive technology speedboat of SCBX Group by investing through SCB 10X  
Venture Capital, exploring new innovations via SCB 10X Tech Labs, and experimenting with advanced 
technologies at SCB 10X R&D.

2025 Guidance  
 
The Thai economy is expected to grow at a rate of 2.4 % by 2025, impacted by Trump 2.0’s trade 
barriers, with a high risk of US import tariffs of Thai exports, including electronic s, automobiles, 
machinery, and computers. Additionally, China’s overcapacity will pressure the competitiveness of Thai 
products, leading to a slowdown in exports. Private investment is expected to recover mo destly. The 
company aims for loan growth of 1-3%, aligning with economic growth. The net interest margin (NIM) 
is projected to be between 3.6- 3.8% based on our base case for one 25 bps policy rate reduction in 
2025. Key variables determining the company’s NIM will depend on growth of high -yield loans in Gen 
2 and the magnitude of debt restructuring the company needs to enter into. Net fee income grow th is 
expected to be 2-4%, mainly driven by the wealth business, a recovery in bancassurance, and  
increased fee contributions from Gen 2 and Gen 3 businesses. 
The cost-to-income ratio is targeted to be between 42-44%, with a continued focus on cost  discipline 
despite expenses related to strategic projects in Cyber Security, Cloud COEs, and ongoing IT spending. 
The credit cost is projected to be between 150-170 bps, factoring in proactive meas ures, a solid risk 
management framework, effective credit cost management practices, and a strong collection  strategy. 
This guidance may change due to economic uncertainties and unforeseen future events.

SCBX Performance in 4Q24 and 2024 (consolidated)  
 
SCBX reported an unaudited consolidated net profit of Baht 43,943 million for 2024, reflecting a year-
over-year increase of 1.0% from Baht 43,521 million in 2023. This growth was mainly driven by higher 
net interest income (NII) due to improved net interest margin (NIM) and lower expected credit losses. 
However, the increase was partially offset by one-off items from the Robinhood trans action, subdued 
fee income, and reduced investment income. 
In the fourth quarter of 2024, net profit rose by 6.5% yoy to Baht 11,7 07 million. This increase was 
mainly driven by higher investment income, increased net fee income, and lower operatin g expenses, 
despite a decline in net interest income.

SCB X Public Company Limited  Management Discussion and Analysis 
 
11 
 
Compared to 3Q24 , net profit rose by 7.0%, mainly due to lower expected credit losses, increased 
investment income, and higher net fee income. However, this growth was partially offset by higher 
operating expenses and a decline in net interest income.

Statutory Capital 
SCBX Financial Group, is subject to the same regulations as the Bank, namely the BOT’s consolidated 
supervision guidelines, and must maintain the same minimum capital requirements including additional 
buffers. The required additional buffers consist of a 2.5% conservation buffer to be held in CET1 and a 
1% Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) buffer.  
SCBX Financial Group follows prudent approach to capital management by maintaining capital  well 
above the minimum regulatory requirements and ensuring adequate loan loss prov isions. This 
additional cushion allows SCBX Financial Group to better handle unforesee n events and absorb any 
emerging risks that may arise from new businesses in the future.
